$comment: Recipe for the recorded half of assets/sfx: excerpts cut from the #GameAudioGDC bundle the operator holds locally (royalty-free, commercial use, modification permitted, no attribution required). Selection rationale and the taxonomy these ids fill are in docs/research/2026-09-07-video-sfx-and-ambience-library.md; the ids are the same ones the generated recipe defines, because the point of this file is to put a real recording behind an id wherever the bundle holds one that is better than a generation. 27 ids here replace a generated sound of the same name and 11 are new. What is deliberately NOT here: every id the bundle cannot serve honestly. There is no stream in it, no night-only cricket bed, and its nearest office room tone is a fridge; those three stay generated rather than be filled with something that is nearly the sound. A ticking-clock BED was cut for the same reason and then dropped: a metronomic event inside a loop announces the wrap on every cycle, which is exactly what qc.event_prominence_db exists to catch, so the clock is here as a single tick instead. No timestamps are written by hand. Beds name a length and the builder sweeps the whole recording for the evenest window of it; one-shots name which event they want and the builder gates the file to find it. 2026-09-10: the recipe was extended from 38 excerpts to 346. The first 38 filled a documentary/explainer taxonomy from the packs that could serve it honestly; the 308 added here are the rest of the bundle, because a 7.5 GB archive sitting unused next to a library that needs sounds is not a curation decision, it is an omission. Most of what the bundle ships is already cut -- 122 packs of two to four sampler files -- so the new entries use the `whole` mode (take the file as delivered, trim, high-pass, level) rather than the event gate: the supplier already decided where the sound starts, and gating over that decision crops whatever swells. `loop` is still used for the 74 long ambiences, which are the only ones with a window left to choose. Categories follow the UCS CatID in the filename where the supplier set one (ANML->animal, AMB->place, WEAP->weapon, VOX->voice/human, CREA-> creature, MAG->magic, DSGN/ROBT->scifi, VEH/TRN/AERO->vehicle, and so on) rather than being re-decided here. One file is deliberately NOT ingested: 'Camp fire, crackling, putting oil in fire, close, night_B-format, Ambix.wav' is 4-channel ambisonic B-format with an unknown channel layout, and `-ac 2` would fold W against the X/Y/Z gradients rather than decode it -- that needs an ambisonic decoder this pipeline does not have, and the same supplier's stereo campfire is already in the library.
